description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing bilateral pulmonary opacities.
description.detailed_description: This is a frontal chest radiograph showing the thorax. There are diffuse bilateral pulmonary opacities, predominantly in the lower lung zones, which may represent consolidation or interstitial involvement. The cardiac silhouette appears normal in size, and there is no obvious pleural effusion. The trachea is midline, and bony structures appear intact.

This is an ultrasound image of the spleen. The organ appears to have a heterogeneous echotexture, with areas of varying echogenicity. The image suggests possible pathology such as infarction, abscess, or other infiltrative processes. The surrounding structures are not clearly visualized in this image.

description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing bilateral pulmonary opacities, 4 weeks after initiation of ART.
description.detailed_description: This is a frontal chest radiograph demonstrating bilateral pulmonary opacities, predominantly in the lower lung zones. The heart size appears within normal limits, and there is no obvious pleural effusion. The opacities may represent infectious or inflammatory processes, potentially related to immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS) following ART initiation. The bony structures and soft tissues are unremarkable.

Case_09008/figure4.jpg.source_caption: H and E stain of hepatic tissue.

description.short_caption: H&E stain of hepatic tissue showing granuloma formation.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows hepatic tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). A well-formed granuloma is visible, characterized by a central collection of inflammatory cells, including epithelioid macrophages and lymphocytes. The surrounding hepatic parenchyma appears disrupted. The granuloma suggests a possible infectious or inflammatory etiology.

Case_09008/figure6.jpg.source_caption: Acid-fast (Ziehl-Neelson) stain of marrow, with cluster of possible acid-fast bacilli.

description.short_caption: Acid-fast (Ziehl-Neelson) stain of bone marrow showing clusters of acid-fast bacilli.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a microscopic view of a bone marrow sample stained with the Ziehl-Neelson technique. The stain highlights clusters of slender, rod-shaped organisms that are acid-fast bacilli, appearing as bright pink or red structures against a blue background. The arrow points to a prominent cluster of these bacilli. The surrounding field shows a mix of cellular and extracellular material typical of bone marrow.
visible_findings: clusters of slender, rod-shaped acid-fast bacilli
pink/red organisms against a blue background

Case_09008/figure5.jpg.source_caption: H and E stain of bone marrow.

description.short_caption: H&E stain of bone marrow showing granulomas and cellular infiltration.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) stain of bone marrow. The field contains granulomas, characterized by clusters of epithelioid histiocytes and multinucleated giant cells, surrounded by lymphocytes and plasma cells. There is evidence of cellular infiltration and disruption of normal marrow architecture. The pink eosinophilic areas represent extracellular matrix and necrotic material, while the dark purple nuclei indicate dense cellularity.

description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing left-sided pleural effusion after 2 months of ART.
description.detailed_description: This is a frontal chest radiograph displaying a significant left-sided pleural effusion, evidenced by the homogenous opacity occupying the lower left hemithorax and obscuring the left costophrenic angle. The mediastinum appears shifted slightly to the right, suggesting mass effect from the effusion. The right lung field appears clear, and there is no visible pneumothorax. The bony structures and soft tissues are unremarkable.
visible_findings: homogenous opacity in the left lower hemithorax
obliteration of the left costophrenic angle

description.short_caption: Chest radiograph after 7 months of ART showing improved lung findings.
description.detailed_description: This is a frontal chest radiograph showing both lung fields, the heart, and the bony thorax. The lung fields appear relatively clear with no obvious consolidations, cavitations, or masses. The cardiac silhouette is within normal limits, and the mediastinum is not widened. The bony structures, including the ribs and clavicles, appear intact. There are no visible pleural effusions or pneumothorax. The findings suggest improvement or resolution of any prior pulmonary abnormalities, consistent with follow-up after antiretroviral therapy (ART).
